extracted.subtask_description: Advice and evaluative guidance for poets about finding and keeping poetic inspiration (the “Muse”) and for shaping poetic practice — emphasizing experience, patience, listening, and the primacy of first impressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure passions with the people
rubrics_metrics.description: “How could poet ever tower, If his passions, hopes, and fears, If his triumphs and his tears, Kept not measure with his people?”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The poet’s passions and sentiments must be commensurate with and rooted in the life of his community — social relevance and sympathy with 'his people' are prerequisites for true poetic stature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value first impressions; avoid over-analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: “second-thoughts are prose; For beauty's acme hath a term as brief As the wave's poise before it break in pearl, Our own breath dims the mirror of the sense.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture the immediate, virginal perception (the sudden flash of feeling or image). Excessive deliberate study or reworking can dull the original vision; the first passionate apprehension often contains the essential poetic truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Muse is elusive; practice patience
rubrics_metrics.description: “Harass her not: thy heat and stir But greater coyness breed in her; Yet thou mayst find, ere Age's frost, Thy long apprenticeship not lost, Learning at last that Stygian Fate Unbends to him that knows to wait.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not force inspiration; endure the long apprenticeship, cultivate discipline, and wait rather than frantically pursue the Muse. Patience and steady craft increase the chance of inspiration returning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live richly — be more than your verse
rubrics_metrics.description: “From fireside lone and trampling street Let thy life garner daily wheat; The epic of a man rehearse, Be something better than thy verse; Make thyself rich, and then the Muse Shall court thy precious interviews.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accumulate concrete, varied life experience (travel, work, relationships, observation). Being 'rich' in living — not merely in technical skill — attracts inspiration; the poet should cultivate a life that supplies material and moral weight to poetry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek inspiration everywhere — high and low
rubrics_metrics.description: “Through mountains, forests, open downs, Lakes, railroads, prairies, states, and towns... Well pleased with logger-camps in Maine As where Milan's pale Duomo lies”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not privilege only classical or elite subjects. Observe factory-wheels, markets, hay-fields, logger-camps, cathedrals — the Muse runs protean across all environments. Diverse settings furnish diverse poetic resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use everyday life as the Muse's material
rubrics_metrics.description: “She spins... With equal care she twines the fates Of cottages and mighty states... Morning and noon and eve supply To her their fairest tints for dye.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend to domestic, ordinary, and quotidian details; they provide the 'tints' and threads that the Muse weaves into art. Everyday routines and small facts of life are legitimate and rich poetic material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate receptive listening and observation
rubrics_metrics.description: “And such enchantment lilt to thee, That thou shalt hear the life-blood flow From farthest stars to grass-blades low, And find the Listener's science still Transcends the Singer's deepest skill!”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop acute powers of listening/observation — the ability to perceive subtle currents of life often outstrips mere technical singing or verbal skill. The craft of attentive perception is crucial to creating deep poetry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pamper the Muse with fresh, unspoiled experiences
rubrics_metrics.description: “Her will I pamper in her luxury: No crumpled rose-leaf of too careless choice Shall bring a northern nightmare to her dreams, ... The invitiate firstlings of experience, Vibrations felt but once and felt life long.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curate and protect the freshness of your experiences; avoid cheapening impressions by careless repetition. Give the Muse 'firstlings' — singular, vivid encounters that retain their power and fuel lasting poetic images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value dynamic, imperfect, surprising forms of art
rubrics_metrics.description: Contrast: “The Grecian gluts me with its perfectness... But ah! this other, this that never ends, Still climbing, luring fancy still to climb... Imagination's very self in stone!”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not privilege only 'perfect', finished forms; appreciate works that are provisional, suggestive, and full of caprice and moral complexity. Art that continually invites imagination and surprise can be more generative for the poet than static perfection.
